RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the October 23, 2008/Kartika 1, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;
Environment and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and Urban
Poverty Alleviation; Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj;
Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and
Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and
Highways; Space; Statistics and Programme
Implementation; Urban Development;
Y outh Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
28
Hotel accommodation for
Commonwealth Games
*81. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  the exact position regarding
availability of approved rooms in both star
and budget category hotels in Delhi as
against reported demand of 50,000
approved rooms, keeping in view the 2010
Commonwealth Games;
(b)  whether DDA has sent any
proposal to his Ministry to increase the
Floor Area Ratio (FAR) of all existing as
well as upcoming hotels in the city;
(c)  if so, whether DDA's proposal has
been approved; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Sharing of information on terror cases
*82. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
 Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Pakistan have
decided to share information on terror cases;
(b)  if so, whether he, recently had a
telephonic conversation with his Pakistani
counterpart to seek revival of the bilateral
dialogue;
(c)  whether during his visit, both
Governments have agreed to fight terror
together;
(d)  if so, whether any agreement in this
regard has been worked out;
(e)  if so, the details thereof; and
(f) to what extent both the countries
have drawn up a plan of  joint action against
terrorism?

29
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Untapped reserves of uranium in
India
*83. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
SHRI N.K. SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that our neclear
plants are presently starved because of non-
availability of uranium;
(b)  if so, whether it is a fact that there
are massive untapped reserves of uranium,
estimated at over 1 lakh tonnes, in the States
of Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Andhra Pradesh,
Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu; and
(c)  the reasons for these reserves having
remained untapped, whereas we have been
pursuing foreign resources?
Traffic condition in cities
†*84. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that traffic
condition has become difficult not only in
big cities but also in small cities due to
increasing  production of buses, scooters,
motorcycles and cars and the usage thereof;
(b)  if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard;
(c)  whether Government would
formulate any national level action plan to
resolve this problem;
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and
(e)  if not,the reasons for not including
it under the Jawaharlal Nehru National
Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) for a
solution?
Schemes to promote sports
*85.  SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
most of the Panchayat areas in the country
are lacking in sports infrastructure;
(b)  if so, whether Government would
consider some specific sports
encouragement scheme at every panchayat
level;
(c)  whether Government would adopt
any specific policy to promote sports at
grass root level; and
(d)  whether Government would
consider to reserve at least 5 per cent
employment for the sportspersons in
Central and State Government and
corporate sector?
LCD production in the country
*86. SHRI PRAKASH JA V ADEKAR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMA TION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government
has decided to encourage Liquid Crystal
Display (LCD) production in the country;
(b)  if so, the details of concessions
offered and its policy, if any; and
(c)  whether Government has instructed
State Governments to offer similar
concessions?

30
Challenges of climate change
*87. SHRI  JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether India, with a coastline of
about 7,500 kms. risks losing a significant
number of lives and assets worth $3.85
trillion due to coastal flooding that may
occur as a result of climate change in 2070,
as per global study conducted by the
Organisation for Economic Cooperation
Development;
(b)  whether the report notes that those
cities with greatest population exposure to
extreme sea levels also tend to be those
with greatest exposure to wind damage from
tropical and extra tropical cyclones; and
(c)  if so, the concrete steps and measures
Government  proposes to take to meet the
challenge of climatic change?
Chinese incursions across LAC
*88. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware of
Chinese incursions across LAC into the
Indian side;
(b)  if so, the facts and details thereof;
(c)  whether Government has taken up
the matter with the Chinese Government;
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and
(e)  the steps taken by Government to
prevent such Chinese incursions?
Japanese cooperation
†*89. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI  MOTILAL VORA:
 Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government has sought
cooperation from Government of Japan to
improve bus service and address housing
problem in Delhi; and
(b)  if so, the reaction of Government of
Japan thereto?
Dumping of household waste in India
*90. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA :
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
the household waste collected weekly
across Britain for recycling is being shipped
and dumped in India;
(b)  if so, the facts and details thereof;
(c)  whether Government proposes to
enact and change the domestic laws and
stop this nefarious and dangerous trade;
and
(d)  if so, the details thereof?
India-Japan Comprehensive Economic
Partnership Agreement
*91. DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA A.
HEPTULLA:
SHRI  MAHENDRA MOHAN:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

31
the India-Japan Comprehensive Economic
Partnership Agreement, that is being
worked on by the two Governments,
would open the floodgates to Japan's
municipal, medical and hazardous wastes
in the country;
(b)  whether Government is also aware
that Japan exported at least 270 tonnes of
toxic waste, including prohibited items such
as zinc ash, lead acid battery wastes and
copper cables coated with the plastic
poison PVC, to India; and
(c)  if so, the details of countries
exporting hazardous waste to India and
what has been done by his Ministry to
address the environmental concerns?
Projects under JNNURM in Nagaland
*92. SHRI KHEKIHO ZHIMOMI:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  the number of projects under the
Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal
Mission (JNNURM) that have been
received from the State of Nagaland, so far;
(b)  the number of projects that have
been approved, so far;
(c)  the grant/Central assistance that has
since been disbursed, project-wise;
(d)  whether CPWD has raised technical
objections to the project relating to the
construction of a shopping complex with
parking at Sewak, whereas similar project
at Mokokchung prepared by the same
agency was approved by the CPWD
without any objections; and
(e)  if so, the details thereof?
Reduction of urban poverty
*93. SHRIMATI  T. RATNA BAI: Will
the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN
POVERTY ALLEVIA TION be pleased to
state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that the rate of
reduction of urban poverty has been far
lower than that of rural poverty;
(b)  if so, the comparative details thereof
during the last four years and the reasons
therefor, especially in coastal and agency
areas of Andhra Pradesh; and
(c) the steps Government would like to
take in future in this regard especially to
remove the poverty among SCs/STs by
uplifting them in the society?
American technology in atomic
energy
†*94. SHRI SHIVANAND TIWARI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government
has given an assurance to America with
regard to awarding contract of establishing
an atomic energy plant of 10,000 MW;
(b)  if so, the facts thereof;
(c)  whether it is also a fact that American
technology is inferior to that of Russia and
France;
(d)  whether it is also a fact that not a
single new reactor has been manufactured
in America during the last two or three
decades; and
(e)  if so, Government's reaction thereto?
Code of conduct for interaction with
MPs
†*95. SHRI  ALI ANWAR ANSARI:
SHRI RAJNITI PRASAD:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government
has issued any circular on resolutions,
orders, instructions and directions regarding
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

32
code of conduct and etiquettes to be
observed  by Government officials while
interacting with  M.Ps and M.L.As and
also while taking necessary action in
response to the letters written by them;
and
(b)  if so, the nature of instructions
issued and complete details thereof?
Stock of uranium
†*96. SHRI  AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a)  the quantum of uranium reserves in
the country;
(b)  whether it is a fact that country is
passing through uranium crisis as a result
of which neclear reactors are likely to be
affected;
(c)  whether Government has conducted
any survey on availability  of atomic and
nuclear minerals in the country; and
(d)  if so, whether Government is
working  on a plan for production of
uranium from country's reserves and their
optimum utilization with a view to achieve
self-reliance in the field of nuclear energy?
Chinese incursions in Indian
territory
*97. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
 Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that China
continues to needle Indian  forces all along
the Line of Actual Control;
(b)  if so, the number of times the
Chinese forces have made incursions in our
territory in Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim
during the current year;
(c)  whether the matter was taken up
with the Chinese Government; and
(d)  if so, the outcome thereof?
Voluntary ban on nuclear tests
†*98. SHRI RAGHUNANDAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the process to lift the one-sided
voluntary ban on nuclear tests which has
been declared in the Indo-US joint
declaration;
(b)  its impact on the Indo-US nuclear
deal, if Government conducts the nuclear
tests by keeping aside the one-sided
voluntary ban; and
(c)  whether Government has received
any assurance from US Government that
fuel supply to nuclear power reactors would
set up consequent upon the nuclear deal
continue unabated even in the situation
when India conducts the neclear test?
Modernization of post offices
†*99.  SHRI  UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is
contemplating to modernize the post
offices in order to accelerate and modernize
the postal system; and
(b)  if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

33
Indians killed in racial violence
†*100. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
fact that many Indians had been killed in
the racial violence that took place in
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,

Africa in the last few days;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
people of Indian community in some cities
of South Africa have been asked to leave
South Africa by winding up their business;
(c) if so, whether Government has taken
up this matter with Government of South
Africa; and
(d) if so, the outcomes thereof?
